title: Crisp Contracts: Hosted LLM Surface PRD and Rollout Rundown
creator: Alex Kim
summary: PRD defining behavioral contracts, acceptance criteria, and a pragmatic launch checklist for the unified hosted endpoints surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). Focus is on deterministic contracts, graceful degradation, and operational runbooks tailored for PLG and enterprise customers.
problem_statement: Customers require predictable behavior and clear failure semantics when integrating generation, chat, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. Existing surface inconsistently documents determinism, fallback behavior, and telemetry requirements which causes integration regressions and operational toil.
goals: Define unambiguous behavioral contracts for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Ship a launch checklist that ensures telemetry, rollout safety gates, and customer-facing documentation are complete
Enable deterministic rollbacks and graded degraded modes without breaking client integrations
Reduce integration incidents by 50% in first 3 months after launch
non_goals: Designing new model architectures or changing model flavors (model onboarding is separate)
Complete overhaul of SDKs (small compatibility shims only)
scope_included: Behavioral contract spec (inputs -> outputs) for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Acceptance tests and eval-set for deterministic checks
API error taxonomy and recommended retry semantics
Runtime telemetry and SLOs: per-token latency, p50/p95/p99, error rates
Rollback playbook and canary gating thresholds
Documentation pages and quickstart examples for each endpoint
scope_out_of: Dedicated or Private deployment feature changes (this PRD targets Hosted only)
Large SDK refactorings or new client libraries
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral spec published with example input/expected output templates for 10 canonical cases across endpoints
Automated acceptance suite (CI) added with pass/fail gates; baseline run passes on staging
Telemetry instrumentation validated: per-route latency, token-cost breakdown, and quality metrics are emitted and visible in Console dashboards
Graceful degradation policy implemented: when performance SLOs violated, requests are automatically routed to compatible model variant with documented semantic differences
Rollback and canary playbooks documented with exact metric thresholds (p95 > 500ms for 5m triggers canary cutback) and automated runbook links
Launch docs and API changelog updated; migration guide for customers that rely on deterministic outputs provided
Security review completed and KMS/Audit logging checklist verified
No P0 outstanding bugs in the core behavioral tests after two full canary waves
rollout_checklist: Staging acceptance tests: run full suite against staging cluster (blocking)
Canary wave 1: 1% production traffic, monitor p95 latency and error-rate for 60m
Canary wave 2: 10% production traffic, hold for 2h, run smoke behavioral diffs on sample traffic
Telemetry sanity: ensure Console shows per-route cost and quality; alerting firing tested
Docs & changelog publish: update hosted-api docs + SDK notes
Support runbook: publish incident playbook, escalation path, and postmortem template
Customer communication: targeted emails to top 50 tenants with migration notes
Post-launch evaluation: collect regression metrics at 24h, 72h, 7d
milestones: Engineering design sign-off and test plan - 2026-03-18
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Behavioral diffs could cause breaking changes for deterministic clients. Mitigation: Publish explicit 'determinism tiers' and provide a compatibility shim to pin previous behavior for 30 days.
Risk: Telemetry gaps delay detection of regressions. Mitigation: Require telemetry parity checklist as blocking for canary progression and run a pre-canary synthetic load test.
Risk: Rollback automation misfires under network partitions. Mitigation: Include manual rollback steps and a separate low-privilege revert path for on-call.
Risk: Customer confusion on fallback semantics. Mitigation: Add explicit endpoint headers that indicate variant and a 'compatibility' field in responses for client checks.
open_questions: Should deterministic mode be opt-in via query param or an endpoint-level setting? (Decision due by 2026-03-16)
What SLAs to promise for fallback responses compared to primary model variants? (PM / Eng alignment needed)
Do we expose a 'compatibility score' in response metadata for embeddings/rerank?
acceptance_test_plan: Create 10 canonical prompts per endpoint covering edge cases and non-deterministic behaviors
Run baseline job that records outputs from current prod and new surface; diffs must be within allowed delta thresholds
Integrate tests into CI with threshold-based fail/warn levels
Add synthetic traffic generator to validate SLOs at target QPS before canary
